title: UiKit component contract metamodel
description: Shape of a component contract INSTANCE. The contract is itself a GTS-typed value: every <component>.contract.instance.json validates against this type, so the metamodel is enforced by the same validator that enforces component props instead of by prose. The props schema the instance points at (props_schema) is a separate GTS type and is not described here.

component_type_ref.description: GTS type id of another kit component. Demo stand-in for x-gts-ref: production writes "x-gts-ref": "gts.frontx.uikit.component.*~" here, which resolves the target in the type registry and fails when no such type is registered. The pattern alone only checks grammar, so a grammatical id for a component that does not exist still needs the registry (in the demo: the directory-existence test).
component_type_ref.$comment: GTS tokens are snake_case; kit directories are kebab-case (navigation_menu -> navigation-menu).

prop_name.description: Name of a prop declared by the component, not a type id. Checked against the extracted prop list by the conformance test.

invariant_id.description: Stable kebab-case handle. Lint findings and evals cite it; never reused after removal.

coverage_verdict.description: "checked-no" (looked at, does not hold) and "not-described" (nobody looked) are different answers and may not collapse into one.

id.description: GTS instance id: this metamodel's type id, then the instance segment. The instance segment carries exactly 5 dot-tokens (frontx.uikit.component.<name>.v<n>).

metamodel.$comment: Version of the overlay vocabulary the compiler emitted, independent of the component's own version.

intent.description: One sentence, the selection-card headline: why the component exists.

use_when.description: Positive selection scenarios. Empty means the component is unselectable, so at least one is required.

dont_use_when.description: A "don't" without a typed alternative leaves the agent with no next move, so `instead` is required and is a type id, not a display name.

anti_patterns.$comment: `instead` here is prose about this component's own API, not a component type ref - the fix stays inside the component.

items.$comment: `why` is required: a counter-example without its reason teaches pattern-matching, not the rule.

props_schema.description: URI of the machine-owned half: the compiled JSON Schema carrying axes, defaults and normative props. Split so the semantic half stays readable and the props half stays a plain provider-safe schema. A derived-type id: the abstract base component type, then the component's own segment, so the pattern also asserts that the props schema really is a child of the base and not a lookalike.
props_schema.$comment: Two segments of 5 dot-tokens each after the fixed `gts.` scheme prefix - the shape gts-ts's Gts.parseSegment accepts (vendor.package.namespace.type.vMAJOR).
